Welcome

What is social innovation?

Social innovation is the process of developing and applying new ideas, services, approaches or ways of working to address social needs. It focuses on people, communities and positive change—not simply on creating something new.

01

Understand people

Listen to communities, observe everyday experiences and identify the needs that are often overlooked.

02

Explore solutions

Use creativity, collaboration and practical thinking to develop solutions that respond to real problems.

03

Create lasting impact

Test ideas, learn from feedback and improve solutions so that they are useful, inclusive and sustainable.

“Small actions, when guided by empathy and commitment, can become the beginning of meaningful change.”

02 / People creating change

Social Innovators

Individuals whose ideas and actions have addressed important social and environmental challenges.

Saalumarada Thimmakka

Environmental conservation · Karnataka

Bio data

Saalumarada Thimmakka was an Indian environmentalist from Karnataka, widely known as the “Mother of Trees.” She came from a modest background and, along with her husband Bikkala Chikkaiah, devoted herself to planting and caring for trees. She received the Padma Shri in 2019 for her contribution to environmental protection.

Contribution to society

She and her husband planted and nurtured hundreds of banyan trees along the road between Hulikal and Kudur, and she is also associated with the planting of thousands of other trees. Her work encouraged people to protect nature and showed how individual effort can create a lasting environmental benefit.

Why and how I am inspired

I am inspired by her patience and dedication towards protecting the environment. Her story teaches me that even a small step, when taken with commitment, can create a big positive change in society.

Source: Saalumarada Thimmakka – background ↗

Aditi Gupta

Menstrual health education · Menstrupedia

Bio data

Aditi Gupta is an Indian social entrepreneur and the co-founder of Menstrupedia. She studied at the National Institute of Design, where her research helped her understand the challenges created by a lack of awareness and conversations around menstruation. She is also a TED speaker and has been recognised for her work in social impact.

Contribution to society

Through Menstrupedia, she uses illustrated educational comics, workshops and other learning resources to explain menstruation and puberty in a simple, friendly way. Her work helps young people, families and educators discuss menstrual health and challenge the stigma surrounding it.

Why and how I am inspired

I admire her courage to speak about a topic that many people hesitate to discuss. She inspires me to use creativity and knowledge to solve real problems and make important information easier for everyone to understand.

Source: Aditi Gupta – Menstrupedia ↗

Harish Hande

Renewable energy · SELCO

Bio data

Dr. Harish Hande is an Indian social entrepreneur and the co-founder of SELCO India, a social enterprise established in 1995. He studied energy engineering at IIT Kharagpur and completed postgraduate and doctoral studies in the United States, focusing on sustainable energy. He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2011.

Contribution to society

Through SELCO, he has worked to make solar energy and reliable lighting more accessible to underserved households and small businesses. His approach connects clean-energy technology with practical financing and local service, helping communities use energy for education, livelihoods and everyday needs.

Why and how I am inspired

I am inspired by how he uses engineering to improve people's everyday lives. As a Computer Science Engineering student, his journey motivates me to think beyond technology itself and focus on how innovation can benefit communities.

Source: Harish Hande – SELCO ↗

Anshu Gupta

Community development · Goonj

Bio data

Anshu Gupta is an Indian social entrepreneur and the founder of Goonj, a non-profit organisation. He is popularly known as the “Clothing Man” for bringing attention to clothing as an important development need. He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2015 for his work.

Contribution to society

Goonj collects and repurposes unused clothing and other urban materials, connecting them with the needs of rural communities. Its initiatives support community-led development by treating people with dignity and recognising local effort, skills and priorities.

Why and how I am inspired

I am inspired by his ability to turn something often considered waste into a useful resource for people. His work reminds me that helping society does not always require something new; sometimes it begins with using what we already have thoughtfully.

Source: Anshu Gupta – Goonj ↗

Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar

Humanitarian work · Art of Living

Bio data

Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar is an Indian spiritual teacher, humanitarian and peace advocate, born in 1956. He founded the Art of Living Foundation in 1981 and later co-founded the International Association for Human Values in 1997. His work focuses on well-being, human values, service and peace.

Contribution to society

Through the Art of Living and associated initiatives, he has promoted yoga, meditation, stress-management programmes, community development, disaster relief and conflict-resolution efforts. These programmes aim to support individuals and communities in building healthier and more peaceful lives.

Why and how I am inspired

I am inspired by his focus on peace, compassion and helping others. His work reminds me that social change is not only about providing resources but also about encouraging understanding, kindness and responsibility towards one another.

Source: Sri Sri Ravi Shankar – Art of Living ↗
